text:
carol: Observed a bunch of route flapping between eu-west and eu-central when spot prices spike for a minute. Users see 2–3x latency variance for short windows. We should discuss adding hysteresis to policy selection rather than pure score argmax.

ben: +1, saw same in trace graphs yesterday. Flap looks like: route A selected -> cost rises -> route B takes traffic -> cost drops -> route A comes back. Oscillation.

dave: Quick thought: add a small time-based sticky bonus that decays (e.g. +penalty if switching within N ms). Keeps current route unless score delta exceeds threshold.

carol: Exactly. Two knobs we could expose in policy DSL: "min_hold_ms" and "switch_delta_pct". Runtime will track last_chosen_route per key and apply ephemeral bonus.

alice: Can we do that without adding large state in the policy engine? One of the goals was to keep policy eval stateless.

ben: We can keep the sticky state in the routing decision cache (short-lived state store) instead of the pure policy evaluator. Policy returns base scores, router layer applies hold logic. That keeps policy DSL small.

carol: Proposal: keep policy semantics as-is (score-only) + introduce routing shim that applies hysteresis. Policy DSL adds opt-in metadata fields so policy authors can annotate routes with stability preferences. Example: {"route_meta": {"stability_pref": "sticky", "min_hold_ms": 5000}}

infra-bot: deploy-check: new routing-shim requires 1 new env var and 2x unit tests.

dave: Tradeoffs: sticky adds route stickiness which can keep traffic pinned to a degraded region during sustained cost spikes. Need graceful fallback/override TTL and emergency preemption if latency SLOs break.

ben: Agreed. We need a safety circuit: if latency > threshold for X samples, forcibly clear hold and re-eval ignoring sticky. Also emit telemetry when preemption happens.

carol: Implementation plan: 1) Add routing-shim service that decorates policy responses at the gateway, 2) Add short-lived last_route cache keyed by tenant+route_key, 3) Expose policy opt-in metadata (string fields), 4) Telemetry hooks for hold/release events, 5) Experiment behind feature flag.

alice: Simulation plan: run the routing sim harness with synthetic cost spikes + region outages, compare churn and downstream SLO impact. Also add unit tests for race windows.

ben: Rollout: dark canary (10% shadow), then gradual enable by tenant, with auto-disable if preemption metric > 0.5% in 10m window. Add a kill-switch in console.

carol: Backwards-compat: default behavior is unchanged unless policy annotates route_meta.stability_pref. So no surprise for existing tenants.

dave: One interface question: where does the shim live? Options: at API gateway (closest to request), at route broker (after capacity decision), or in runtime. My preference: gateway-level to minimize cross-service coordination.

ben: Gateway-level seems easiest for rollout and for observability per request. But we'll need to ensure it has low-latency access to last_route cache (in-memory with local replication + redis fallback).

carol: Observability: emit these fields in traces: chosen_route, held_since, hold_reason, override_count. Also track metric: route_switch_rate per tenant+region.

infra-bot: perf-note: adding one memcache lookup per decision will add ~0.5ms P50. Need perf bench.

alice: Action items: @dave prototype shim and cache design; @ben add telemetry + sim scenarios; @carol update policy DSL proposal text and RFC; @infra-bot create bench job.

carol: I'll open a short RFC follow-up doc and link it here. Quick question: any objections to the gateway-first approach?

ben: No objections. small caveat: define clear preemption thresholds.

dave: No blockers from infra. I'll start a spike tomorrow.

carol: Great. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
